To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the end-of-life care in the West has evolved from the traditional model of care to the modern model of palliative care.

(i) the end-of-life care issues are not well addressed in India, (ii) there is a lack of education and training of the medical and nursing professionals in this area, (iii) there is lack of public awareness and (iv) there is lack and absence of case law in the country.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the end-of-life care of patients in India.
the end-of-life decision-making and the ethical and social issues involved in the process.
the end-of-life decisions in the Indian context, and how they can be made more effective.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Indian approach should be a blend of the Western and the Eastern approach.
there is a need to develop an Indian perspective on the end-of-life issue, which will be relevant in the Indian context.
the Indian experience is not yet mature to make such a statement.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Indian society has to prepare itself for the end-of-life challenges.
end-of-life issues are a reality and will be more common in the future and the Indian society needs to face this reality.
we should learn from the West but not blindly follow their methods.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the end-of-life decisions are best made by the patient in consultation with his/her physician and family members.
end-of-life issues are not just a medical problem, but also a societal problem.
the end-of-life decisions should not be made in isolation but as a part of the continuum of the patient's care and that it is not possible to have a single approach to the end-of life care.
